title: Prompting for Developers
description: Learn to use role, task, and constraint-driven prompting to generate high-quality, production-ready code with Claude.
learning_objectives: Define a specific professional persona for the AI to improve output quality
Structure prompts using the Role-Task-Constraint framework
Apply technical constraints to minimize hallucinations and ensure compatibility
Iteratively refine AI-generated code through targeted feedback loops
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with an LLM interface (e.g., Claude or ChatGPT)

sections.heading: The Anatomy of a Developer Prompt
sections.content_brief: Explain why generic prompts produce generic, often unusable code. Introduce the Role-Task-Constraint framework as the standard for professional software engineering prompts.
sections.code_context: A side-by-side comparison of a 'naive' prompt versus a 'structured' developer prompt.

sections.heading: Defining the Persona (The Role)
sections.content_brief: Discuss how assigning a specific role (e.g., 'Senior Staff Engineer' or 'Security Auditor') shifts the AI's priority toward best practices, scalability, and edge-case handling.
sections.code_context: Examples of how changing the role from 'Coder' to 'Performance Optimization Expert' changes the resulting code implementation.

sections.heading: Precision in Task Definition
sections.content_brief: Cover the importance of explicit inputs and outputs. Teach developers how to define the exact scope of a function, including expected data types and return values.
sections.code_context: A prompt that defines a specific interface for input/output to ensure the AI generates type-safe code.

sections.heading: Applying Hard Constraints
sections.content_brief: Detail how to use constraints to enforce library versions, coding standards (e.g., PEP8), and architectural limitations (e.g., 'no external dependencies').
sections.code_context: A prompt that forces the AI to use a specific version of a library and avoid deprecated methods.

sections.heading: The Iterative Refinement Loop
sections.content_brief: Explain how to treat the first output as a draft. Provide strategies for giving corrective feedback on edge cases, bugs, or style violations without restarting the conversation.
sections.code_context: A sequence of follow-up prompts that refine a piece of code to handle an overlooked null pointer exception.

admonitions.content: When applying constraints, list them as a bulleted list. LLMs process structured lists more reliably than long paragraphs of requirements.
Never assume AI-generated code is secure by default. Always perform a manual security review or run the code through a static analysis tool before merging to production.
